summary: Canadian Coast Guard light at the entrance to Ucluelet Harbour: first lit in 1906, tower rebuilt in 1915, automated since 1988.

structures.note: Present structure, per the marker; material not given in the sources read.

access.note: The Lighthouse Loop of the Wild Pacific Trail, which starts from parking on Coast Guard Road, offers views of the light. No source invites visitors into the tower.

events.note: Pass of Melfort lost; the marker and the Ucluelet and Area Historical Society tie the first lighthouse to it. The Department of Marine reports consulted do not name the ship.
Red whistling buoy established in the Carolina Channel, off Amphitrite point.
Wooden tower; the Department's annual report records a light established on the extremity of the point.
Fixed white light, elevated 60 feet (18 m) above high water, visible 13 miles (the report gives miles).
Storm waves destroyed the wooden lighthouse, per the marker.
Replaced by the present structure, per the marker.
Maintained by on-site personnel until 1988, when the Canadian Coast Guard automated many of its lights; Amphitrite Point was one of them.

keepers.name: George Fraser
keepers.note: Listed against Amphitrite point in the Department's 1906 keepers' list (39th annual report, printed p. 176). Appointed 2 April 1906 at a listed salary of $240; the row was read on the page image (scan p. 185).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record's conflict: Wikidata gives 1915 and Rowlett gives 1906. The Department of Marine's annual report records a light established on the point in 1906; the marker and the Ucluelet and Area Historical Society give 1915 for the present tower.

notes_for_editor: The 1906 keepers' list (39th report, printed p. 176, scan p. 185) was checked on the page image: the row reads Fraser, George | Amphritrite | April 2, 1906 | $240, so the appointment date is stated in the story. The 1908 keepers' table is too garbled to confirm Fraser for later years, so the story names only the 1906 listing. The Pass of Melfort wreck (1905) rests on the marker and the Ucluelet and Area Historical Society; the Department of Marine text cached in the corpus has no mention of the ship. The 1914 destruction and 1915 rebuilding rest on the marker alone among primary-type sources read here; the 1915-16 Department report summary records two concrete towers erected in British Columbia that year without naming the stations, so it is not cited. The record's focal height (15.2 m) and nominal range (15 NM) come from the Coast Guard list, entry 135, which the earlier note wrongly said gave neither; the 1906 notice gives 60 feet above high water and 13 miles, not stated as nautical miles, so the story does not compare them. The Wikipedia article was not cited. Records: the record's 1915 date conflicts with the 1906 first light, as resolved above. No newspaper or heritage register was searched for this station.
